findings.title: SignalEvent leaks AttributeError for malformed timestamp meanings
findings.description: `SignalEvent.__post_init__` checks `self.time.meaning is not TimeMeaning.AVAILABLE_AT` and then formats the failure with `self.time.meaning.value`. `Timestamp` only validates `ns` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:54-58`; it does not validate `meaning`. Thus runtime callers can pass `Timestamp(100, "available_at")`, `Timestamp(100, 5)`, or `Timestamp(100, None)`, which are accepted by `Timestamp`, fail the identity check at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:76`, and then raise `AttributeError` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:79` instead of `InvalidSignalError`. That breaks the slice contract that anything other than `AVAILABLE_AT` raises `InvalidSignalError`. Validate that `meaning` is a `TimeMeaning` instance first, and format malformed values without assuming `.value`.

findings.title: Signal rejection tests omit malformed meaning values
findings.description: The parametrized rejection cases at `tests/core_model/test_signals.py:79-92` cover a non-`Timestamp`, wrong `TimeMeaning` enum members, and a float `ns`, but there is no case for a `Timestamp` whose `meaning` is a plain string, integer, or `None`. Because `Timestamp` permits those field values (`src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:54-58`) and the new validation path is at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:76-80`, add parametrized cases asserting `InvalidSignalError` for those malformed meanings. Without this regression test, the crash described above is not caught by the suite.

findings.title: Confidence test helpers use loose NumPy array annotations
findings.description: `_array` and `_mask` at `tests/core_model/test_confidence.py:69-74` return bare `np.ndarray`, while strict Pyright includes tests (`pyproject.toml:39-44`). The surrounding suite uses precise NumPy annotations, for example `NDArray[np.int64]`, `NDArray[np.float64]`, and `NDArray[np.bool_]` at `tests/core_model/test_labels.py:44-53`, and parameterized `np.ndarray[...]` forms at `tests/core_model/test_timestamps.py:119` and `tests/core_model/test_timestamps.py:162`. Bare `np.ndarray` erases dtype/shape information and can introduce partially unknown types under strict checking; use `NDArray[np.float64]` and `NDArray[np.bool_]` here.
